paragraphs.title: Making the Covenant and Purifying the Temple

answers: All the elders of Judah and Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The king gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
easy.q: Whom did the king gather to himself?

answers: In the house of the LORD
easy.explanation: He read the book in the house of the LORD.
easy.q: Where did the king read the words of the book of the covenant?

answers: They offered sacrifices in high places
easy.explanation: The text says, “And all the people stood to the covenant.”
easy.q: What did all the people do after the king made the covenant?

answers: To walk after the LORD and keep His commandments
medium.explanation: He promised to walk after the LORD and keep His commandments, testimonies, and statutes.
medium.q: What did the king promise in the covenant?

answers: They were brought out and burned
They were placed beside the altar
medium.explanation: The vessels were brought out of the temple and burned without Jerusalem.
medium.q: What did the king command to be done with the vessels made for Baal and the grove?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes wholehearted and complete commitment.
medium.q: What does “with all their heart and all their soul” express?

answers: The covenant renewal was a public national event
The event took place only at Bethel
challenge.explanation: Many leaders and all the people participated.
challenge.q: What does the presence of elders, priests, prophets, and all the people show?

answers: Reading declared what they promised to obey
Reading was only for the priests
challenge.explanation: The people heard the covenant’s words before pledging to keep them.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between reading the covenant book and making the covenant?

answers: The vessels were burned, the people gathered, and the book was read
The covenant was made, the elders gathered, and the book was read
The people gathered, the book was read, the covenant was made, and the temple was cleansed
challenge.explanation: This is the order presented in the passage.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the events?

paragraphs.title: Abolishing High Places and Foreign Worship in Judah

easy.explanation: The king defiled the high places and broke them down.
easy.q: What did the king do to Judah’s high places?

answers: Making children pass through the fire to Molech
easy.explanation: Topheth was defiled so that no one could sacrifice a son or daughter to Molech.
easy.q: What practice was stopped at Topheth?

answers: He placed it in the Temple
easy.explanation: He burned it, stamped it to powder, and scattered the powder.
easy.q: What did the king do with the grove from the house of the LORD?

answers: They were priests of the high places
medium.explanation: The passage specifically says that the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar.
medium.q: Why did the priests of the high places not come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem?

answers: Made it unfit for religious use
medium.explanation: To defile it was to make it polluted and unusable for worship.
medium.q: What does “defiled” mean in “he defiled Topheth”?

answers: They abolished centers of idolatrous worship
medium.explanation: Each action removed or polluted a place or object connected with false worship.
medium.q: What did the actions against the grove, Topheth, and the sun altars have in common?

answers: They represent the variety of foreign worship that was abolished
They describe the building of the Temple
challenge.explanation: They were objects of worship whose service Josiah ended.
challenge.q: Why are the sun, moon, planets, and host of heaven mentioned?

answers: The reform reached worship centers throughout Judah
The priests were sent to Egypt
challenge.explanation: The reform extended from Geba to Beer-sheba.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from bringing all the priests out of Judah’s cities?

answers: The grove was burned and pulverized, while the houses were broken down
The grove was placed in the Temple, while the houses were rebuilt
Nothing was done to either one
challenge.explanation: The grove was burned and reduced to powder; the houses were broken down.
challenge.q: What difference is shown between the treatment of the grove and the houses of the sodomites?

answers: The altar made by Jeroboam son of Nebat
easy.explanation: The altar was made by Jeroboam, who made Israel to sin.
easy.q: Whose altar did Josiah destroy at Bethel?

easy.explanation: Josiah took away the houses of the high places.
easy.q: What did Josiah do to the houses of the high places in Samaria’s cities?

easy.explanation: He said, “Let no man move his bones.”
easy.q: Whose bones did Josiah command the people not to move?

answers: By burning bones upon the altar and polluting it
By moving the sepulchre to Jerusalem
medium.explanation: He burned bones upon the altar, fulfilling the proclaimed word.
medium.q: How did Josiah fulfill the word of the man of God?

answers: The men identified him as the prophet who came from Samaria
Josiah could not find the grave
medium.explanation: The men said it was the sepulchre of the prophet who came from Samaria.
medium.q: Why were the bones of the other prophet left alone?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that it was crushed and pulverized.
medium.q: What does “stamped it small to powder” mean?

answers: Both actions polluted and abolished the altar
Both actions preserved the altar’s worship
challenge.explanation: The altar was broken down, burned, and polluted with bones.
challenge.q: What connection is there between destroying the altar and burning bones upon it?

answers: He recognized prophetic authority and acted according to it
He believed prophecy belonged only to Samaria
challenge.explanation: Josiah fulfilled the prophecy and respected the prophet’s grave.
challenge.q: What does preserving the prophet’s sepulchre show about Josiah?

answers: He destroyed the altar, identified the sepulchre, and burned the bones
He identified the sepulchre, built the high place, and burned the grove
He destroyed the altar and high place, burned the grove and bones, and preserved the prophet’s bones
challenge.explanation: This sequence summarizes the events in the passage.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes Josiah’s actions at Bethel?

paragraphs.title: Josiah’s Passover and Loyalty to the Torah

answers: Keep the passover unto the LORD
Build a high place in Samaria
easy.explanation: He commanded the people to keep the passover unto the LORD.
easy.q: What did Josiah command the people to do?

easy.explanation: The Passover was held unto the LORD in Jerusalem.

answers: Familiar spirits, wizards, images, idols, and abominations
easy.explanation: He removed these forms of divination and idolatry.
easy.q: Which practices did Josiah put away?

answers: According to the book of the covenant
According to the men of Samaria
medium.explanation: It was kept as written in the book of the covenant.
medium.q: According to what did Josiah command the Passover to be kept?

answers: It was the first Passover ever held
It was an unusually remarkable Passover
medium.explanation: No such Passover had been held from the days of the judges and earlier kings.
medium.q: What does the comparison with earlier Passovers emphasize?

answers: To carry out what was written in the law
medium.explanation: Josiah acted so that the written law would be obeyed.
medium.q: What does “perform the words of the law” mean?

answers: Both expressed a return to worship according to God’s law
challenge.explanation: The Passover followed the covenant book, while false worship was removed.
challenge.q: How were the Passover and the removal of divination connected?

answers: He was faithful only during Passover
No king was like him in turning to the LORD with all his heart, soul, and might
challenge.explanation: The passage gives Josiah exceptional praise for his devotion to the LORD.
challenge.q: What does the passage emphasize about Josiah’s faithfulness?

challenge.explanation: It was held in the eighteenth year of King Josiah.
challenge.q: In what year of Josiah’s reign was this Passover held?

paragraphs.title: Judgment on Judah and Josiah’s Death

answers: He did not turn from His great wrath against Judah
He did not read the covenant book
easy.explanation: The LORD did not turn from the fierceness of His wrath against Judah.
easy.q: What did the LORD not do despite Josiah’s righteousness?

easy.explanation: Josiah went against Pharaoh-nechoh, and Pharaoh killed him at Megiddo.
His servants carried him to Jerusalem and buried him there.

answers: Because of the provocations of Manasseh
Because the people did not go to the Temple
Because Josiah did not keep Passover
medium.explanation: The LORD’s anger was connected with the provocations of Manasseh.
medium.q: Why did the judgment remain upon Judah?

answers: To meet the king of Judah
To meet the men of Bethel
medium.explanation: Josiah went against Pharaoh-nechoh at Megiddo.
medium.q: Why did Josiah go to Megiddo?

answers: To reject and cast Judah away
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Judah’s rejection and removal from the LORD’s presence.
medium.q: What does “remove Judah also out of my sight” mean?

answers: Josiah is faithful to the LORD, yet judgment on Judah remains
Josiah worships idols, yet the people are faithful
Pharaoh-nechoh supports Judah, yet Josiah refuses
challenge.explanation: Josiah is praised, but the judgment against Judah is not withdrawn.
challenge.q: What central tension appears in these verses?

answers: He was buried in Jerusalem, went to Megiddo, and Jehoahaz became king
He went against Pharaoh-nechoh, was killed at Megiddo, and was buried in Jerusalem
Jehoiakim became king, Josiah died in Egypt, and he was buried in Samaria
challenge.explanation: This is the order recorded in the passage.
challenge.q: Which sequence describes the end of Josiah’s life?

answers: Judah would always remain separate from Israel
The LORD would restore Israel to Judah
Judah’s removal would be like Israel’s removal
challenge.explanation: The LORD says He will remove Judah as He removed Israel.
challenge.q: What comparison is made between Judah and Israel?

paragraphs.title: Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim under Egyptian Rule

easy.explanation: Jehoahaz reigned three months in Jerusalem.
easy.q: How long did Jehoahaz reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: Pharaoh-nechoh put him in bands and took him away to Egypt.
Pharaoh-nechoh turned Eliakim’s name to Jehoiakim.
easy.q: What name did Pharaoh-nechoh give Eliakim?

medium.explanation: The passage says that Jehoahaz did evil in the sight of the LORD.
medium.q: What did Jehoahaz do in the sight of the LORD?

medium.explanation: He taxed the land to provide the money demanded by Pharaoh.
medium.q: Why did Jehoiakim collect silver and gold from the people?

answers: He divided the land into cities
He assessed the people and required payment
medium.explanation: The people were charged according to their taxation to pay Pharaoh.
medium.q: What does “he taxed the land” mean in this context?

challenge.explanation: Pharaoh removed Jehoahaz and made Eliakim king instead.
challenge.q: What does the change from Jehoahaz to Jehoiakim show about Pharaoh-nechoh’s power?

answers: Jehoiakim was removed, Jehoahaz was crowned, and Pharaoh arrived
Jehoahaz was crowned, taken to Egypt, and replaced by Jehoiakim
Pharaoh was crowned, Jehoahaz collected tribute, and Jehoiakim was exiled
challenge.explanation: The people made Jehoahaz king; Pharaoh took him away and appointed Jehoiakim.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence of the change in rule?

answers: Jehoahaz reigned briefly, while Jehoiakim reigned eleven years
Jehoahaz reigned eleven years, while Jehoiakim reigned three months
challenge.explanation: Jehoahaz reigned three months, while Jehoiakim reigned eleven years.
challenge.q: What major difference is given between the reigns of Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim?
